title: Spreken
subtitle: Talking about yourself in depth
intro: In this lesson you will learn to tell your life story in more depth: where you were born, where you grew up and what you want for the future. You will review the main tenses, modal verbs and subordinate clauses so you can explain reasons and wishes in longer sentences. By the end you can introduce yourself in detail and ask friendly follow-up questions.

grammar.title: Review: present, perfect, simple past and future
grammar.explanation: You already know four main ways to talk about your life. Use the **present** for now and habits, the **perfect** for finished actions that matter now, and the **simple past** for background and finished moments in a story. For plans use **gaan + infinitive**; for promises and predictions use **zullen + infinitive**. The infinitive goes at the end.

rows: Vroeger woonde ik in een dorp.

examples.nl: Ik ben in een klein dorp opgegroeid.
examples.en: I grew up in a small village.
In the past I lived in Germany.

examples.nl: Later ga ik in Nederland werken.
examples.en: Later I am going to work in the Netherlands.

grammar.tip: In a story, the perfect opens the scene and the simple past gives details: Ik ben naar Utrecht verhuisd. Toen was ik nog jong.

grammar.title: Review: modal verbs and te-constructions
grammar.explanation: Modal verbs such as **kunnen, willen, mogen** and **moeten** go second and send the infinitive to the end. Do not use **te** after a modal: **Ik wil leren**, not *Ik wil te leren*. Some verbs take **te** or **om ... te**: **hopen te**, **proberen te**, **vergeten te**, **van plan zijn om ... te**. The **te**-infinitive also goes at the end.

rows: Ik wil later in Nederland werken.
Ik hoop ooit terug te komen.
Ik ben van plan om te verhuizen.

examples.nl: Ik hoop ooit in Nederland te werken.
examples.en: I hope to work in the Netherlands one day.

examples.nl: Ik probeer elke dag Nederlands te spreken.
examples.en: I try to speak Dutch every day.

examples.nl: Ik ben van plan om te verhuizen.

grammar.tip: If the verb already has a modal, drop te: Ik wil leren, Ik moet werken.

grammar.title: Review: subordinate clauses with dat, omdat, als and toen
grammar.explanation: After **dat, omdat, als** and **toen**, all verbs go to the end of the clause. **Als** means 'if' or 'when' for the present, future or repeated situations. **Toen** means 'when' for a specific situation or period in the past, not for repeated situations. If the subordinate clause comes first, the main clause starts with the verb: **Toen ik klein was, woonde ik in een dorp.**

grammar.tip: Ask: a specific past situation? Use toen. Present, future or repeated? Use als.

culture.title: Toen = when, for a specific past situation
culture.text: In Dutch, **toen** means 'when' when you talk about a specific situation or period in the past: **Toen ik hier kwam, ...** / **Toen ik klein was, ...** For repeated past situations, Dutch often uses **als** or **wanneer**: **Als ik vroeger bij mijn oma was, ...** In the present or future, use **als**: **Als ik later geld heb, ...** If the **toen**- or **als**-clause comes first, the main clause starts with the verb: **Toen ik klein was, woonde ik in een dorp.**

summary: Use the present, perfect and simple past to tell your life story; use gaan and zullen for plans and expectations.
After dat, omdat, als and toen, put all verbs at the end of the clause.
Use toen for a specific past situation; use als for the present, future or repeated situations.
Modal verbs take the infinitive at the end without te; hopen, proberen and van plan zijn use te or om ... te.
